content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I have a private windmill managed by a [product_name] controller from a manufacturer that went bankrupt three years ago. I’m trying to update the windvane programming to a new model and function by extracting the current code from the purple copy-protected memory card and reprogramming it using [product_name] PC software, but I’m struggling. I have the correct password but don't understand how to retrieve the program from the card into the PC tool.

Hi. Could you clarify what you mean by "LS"? Is this a PLC brand? What type of card do you have—SD or cartridge? Sharing the part number of your [product_name] controller, or a photo of the device with the card, could help us assist you. I’ve attached a section from the System Manual. Please check if this helps. Let us know with some feedback.

Sorry, the [product_name] in use is [article_no], which has an older memory card, not an SD. By LS, I mean [product_name] software—the PC programming tool. This forum is excellent, and responses are really fast.

Hi [user_name]. Perhaps our contributor [user_name] refers to something in Figure 05, but I’m not sure about LS—let’s see if more details are provided. Memory/battery cards can be used with certain [product_name] controllers.
Hello [user_name], Sorry for any overlap. Can you share what you currently have: software, cables, or anything else?

I've read the attached [document]. If I’m correct, the steps are: 1) Copy the card contents into the [product_name] controller; 2) Remove the card; 3) Connect a USB cable to the card slot; 4) Copy the controller contents to the PC. At which point should the password be entered?

That sounds accurate. Your PC should prompt for the password once the upload process (controller to PC) starts. Please note—the uploaded program may appear unorganized, so you’ll need to restructure the code blocks. You can work with multiple pages and use the cut tool to redirect wires to page markers. If this works, let us know and consider rating [user_name]'s helpful message.
Here’s the issue: When I unplug the memory card, the controller pauses for a few seconds and then shows 'no program', meaning there’s nothing available to upload once I connect the cable.

Hello [user_name], wait a moment. You copy the memory card into the [product_name] controller—what happens if you leave it in? Is the program loaded on the controller? Try checking the display for any blocks.

Are we sure the [product_name] controller operates when the card is inserted? I suggest repeating the previous steps: keep the card inserted after loading; turn the power off, then on; confirm the program is present; try uploading again.

Sorry, I'm new to [product_name] controllers but have used other PLCs before. When entering 'edit program', I’m asked for the password and everything seems fine—I can view the blocks and details. Copying from the card to the controller appears successful, with no errors. However, when copying, it doesn’t ask for a password, only when editing the program. I’d expect it to prompt for the password during copying as well. Also, if I remove the card, regardless of whether the power is on, the program disappears from the controller, likely due to copy-protect settings. Furthermore, when powering up the controller with an empty memory and the card in the slot, it runs the program from the card automatically instead of copying it internally. I’m also concerned about losing the program on the card since it’s the only copy I have.

Did you look at the [document] I posted earlier? I haven’t worked with these memory cards before, but I strongly suspect you’d need to remove the copy-protect function. You’re welcome to wait for more experienced users to help, or try asking in the German-language forum, where there’s more activity among [product_name] users. If it’s urgent, consider submitting a support request. I have no further suggestions for now—please let us know when it’s resolved. Best of luck.
Hello [user_name], If you want to try, be careful: If you're reading a program via PC, make sure to SAVE before proceeding. There are ways to overwrite a password-protected program in [product_name].

Thank you very much for your support. The [document] states that if it's copy-protected and has a password, copying should be possible. I just don't understand the process. If you could post this issue in the German forum, I’d appreciate it.
Hello [user_name], If you want to access the German forums, click the "Deutsch" option at the top. That should let you post in German; test it out, or ask the moderators if needed.
Just for reference, I’m using [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no].

Please note: If copy protection is active, removing the card will delete the program from the controller. Here’s how to retrieve the program: 1. Disable copy protection; 2. You can then remove the card and the controller will retain the program; 3. Now use the programming cable to upload the program. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are working to transfer a program from a legacy, copy-protected memory card in a [product_name] controller to a PC using [product_name] programming software. New users are unclear on the hardware and software steps for bypassing copy protection, entering the password, and preventing program loss. The main concern is sequencing these actions correctly to avoid losing the only program copy and ensuring a successful upload.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a clear, step-by-step guide for safely extracting and copying a protected program from the [product_name] memory card to the PC via [product_name] software, including instructions for password entry and hardware handling.
